_readme: THE FLOW MODEL. The Router's state machine, declared as data.
This file is the single source of truth for how a player moves between screens, and it
is not documentation: tests/integration/test_flow_model.gd drives every edge below
through the real world scene, records what EventBus.flow_changed actually emitted, and
fails if the recording differs from the `trace` written here. A model nothing checks is
a comment that rots, which is why this sits beside mutants.tsv rather than in docs/.
UPDATE THIS FILE BEFORE CHANGING FLOW CODE, not after. It exists because the knowledge
of what a transition passes THROUGH lived only in five milestones' worth of scattered
code, and the question nobody asked - what does this new edge go through? - shipped a
Continue button that replayed the game's opening conversation over the loaded save.
WHAT A TRACE IS. The exact sequence of flow_changed events an action may emit, in order.
Most edges are one hop. Two are not, and both are real rather than accidents:
- a defeat is battle -> world -> game_over, because _close_battle runs before
open_game_over: the fight screen is torn down first so two full-screen views are
never stacked.
- leaving a game over for the title is game_over -> world then world -> title, for the
same reason one step earlier.
An EMPTY trace is a legal answer and means the action changed no state at all. The one
that surprises people: a warp re-enters a map from WORLD, and WORLD to WORLD is not a
change.
WHAT AN INVARIANT IS. A named fact that must hold while the machine is in that state,
asserted after every arrival. The names are resolved by the suite, so a vertex naming an
invariant nothing implements fails the build rather than passing silently.
WALKS. Since M31 the same edges are also driven in SEQUENCES: six seeded walks of
twenty-four steps, on one world that is never rebuilt between them, asserting the same
trace and the same invariants after every step. Per-edge checking is silent about
anything that only goes wrong on a second visit - it found a pause screen and a shop
screen that were closed but never freed, and went on eating the key that opens them.
A failing walk is minimised by tests/helpers/flow_walk.gd before it is reported, so the
message names the shortest sequence that still fails rather than the one chance drew.
Every walkable edge must be driven by one of the seeds, which is asserted: a random walk
that never reaches a game over would report green otherwise. `boot` is not walkable - it
describes the process opening, not an action - and the per-edge gate still checks it.
NOT REACHABLE IN PRODUCTION, on purpose: no overlay opens over another. The stack
supports it (test_router.gd proves that) and world_scene never does it, because
_unhandled_input refuses world input unless the state is WORLD.

title.about: The screen a run is started from. No game is built behind it.

world.about: The only state the player moves in.

dialog.about: A conversation is open; movement is suspended.

paused.about: The menu is open over the world.

battle.about: A fight has the screen; the world is still there underneath.

shop.about: A counter is open over the live world.

resting.about: A night is passing. Nothing to press; it ends on its own.

saving.about: A save point is open: the slot list, and nothing else on it. Reached from a conversation under either save policy, which is why it is its own state rather than the pause menu jumped to a page - a priest does not hand you your equipment.

game_over.about: The run ended. The ways on are a save, a fresh start, or the title.

edges.note: The process opens on the title, so nothing has changed yet.
Announced only since M23: enter_map's reset used to assign the state field.

Goes through boot_from_save, NEVER through the start map. The bug this whole model exists because of was an extra world -> dialog hop right here, from the start map's entry hooks firing on the way past.
Driven by the real cancel key, because the guard that makes PAUSED reachable only from WORLD lives in _unhandled_input and nowhere else.
Opened DEFERRED from a dialog effect, so the adapter waits a frame.
The screen ends itself; nothing presses anything.
Opened DEFERRED from a dialog effect, the open_shop rule, so the adapter waits a frame.
TWO hops, and the middle one is real: _close_battle runs before open_game_over so two full-screen views are never stacked.
Two hops for the same reason. The from used to read world because to_title reset first; M23 made it say where it came from.
One hop: the close pops to world and start_game's reset finds it already there.
Changes the map, not the state. The empty trace is the point: a listener woken by every doorway is a listener nobody can use.
